payload.title: Async optimizer transport, so deferred learning truly overlaps provider calls
payload.description:
Follow-up from flywheelb2 (PR #15).

Current: OptimizerAgent.propose() calls its completion transport synchronously from inside async optimization (flywheel.py improve, staged_optimization.py, control_scheduler.py, idea_screening.py). With learning="deferred", Cyclotron.learn() releases the store lock between outputs, but each optimizer provider call still blocks the event loop, so reviews and decisions in the same process cannot run while a call is in flight.

Constraint found: the call cannot simply move to a thread (asyncio.to_thread). DecisionFlywheel wraps optimizer.observer (flywheel.py ~197-203) so optimizer-request/response events are written to the wheel's SQLite connection; SQLite connections are bound to their creating thread (check_same_thread) and the wheel and cyclotron share no write lock across threads. Writes must stay on the event-loop thread.

Desired: an async optimizer transport (e.g. an awaitable complete, or OptimizerAgent.propose_async) used by every optimization path when available, with observer events still emitted on the loop thread before and after the awaited provider call. Synchronous transports keep working unchanged.

Acceptance: with an awaiting fake transport, a review (and a decide) issued while learn() is inside a provider call completes before that call returns; no SQLite access happens off the loop thread (spec asserts thread identity in the observer); optimizer call limits and recorded optimizer-request/response events are unchanged; synchronous transports behave exactly as today.
